Anthropic Model Case Study Series · Consolidated Lineage 🗂️

The Claude Lineage: A Consolidated Comparison, Claude 1 to Fable 5.1

This series wrote full case studies for Claude 1 and Claude 2. Rather than a dedicated article for every release since, this piece lines up the entire Claude lineage — Claude 2.1, the Claude 3 family, Claude 3.5, Claude 3.7, the Claude 4 family, the 4.x and 5.x point releases, and the new Mythos-class Fable/Mythos tier — across the same eight dimensions this series uses throughout, and closes with a direct comparison to the GPT lineage this site has also documented in full.

FL
FrontierAGI Team
September 16, 2026 · 80 min read
Opening Full Timeline Claude 1 & 2 2.1 → 3.7 Claude 4 → 4.5 Sonnet/Opus 5 → Fable 5.1 Cross-Cutting Threads Claude vs. GPT What Stayed Constant Readiness Checklist What's Missing References Videos Verdict

A Lineage Defined by What It Never Disclosed

This site's GPT lineage comparison found a trend: disclosure declined over time, from GPT-1's precise "one month, 8 GPUs" to GPT-6 Astra's near-total opacity. Claude's lineage has no such arc — because Anthropic never disclosed parameter counts, architecture, or training compute for any Claude model, including the very first one. What did change, repeatedly and dramatically, was capability, safety framework maturity, and the shape of the product itself.

Era 1 — Claude 2.1 to Claude 3.7 Sonnet

The Multi-Tier Lineup and the First Reasoning Fork

Nov 2023Claude 2.1
Scaffolding shift: doubled the shipped context window to 200,000 tokens and reduced hallucination rates — the last single-tier Claude release before Anthropic split the lineup by capability and cost.
Mar 4, 2024Claude 3 family — Opus, Sonnet, Haiku
Architecture and product shift: Anthropic's first genuinely multi-tier lineup, all three sharing a 200,000-token context window and, for the first time, vision (image input) capability. Opus led on knowledge and reasoning benchmarks (MMLU, GPQA, GSM8K), Sonnet balanced speed and intelligence, Haiku targeted near-instant responses — the same three-tier shape (frontier / balanced / fast) OpenAI's GPT-5.6 family would later adopt with Sol/Terra/Luna.
Jun 2024Claude 3.5 Sonnet
Benchmark shift: outperformed the larger Claude 3 Opus on most benchmarks (59.4% GPQA, 92% HumanEval) at a fraction of the cost, and introduced Artifacts — a dedicated side panel for generated code, documents, and designs the user can edit in place.
Oct–Nov 2024Claude 3.5 Sonnet (updated) + Claude 3.5 Haiku
Agentic scaffolding shift: the updated 3.5 Sonnet introduced computer use in public beta and jumped SWE-bench Verified from 33% to 49% — higher than any other publicly available model at the time. Claude 3.5 Haiku shipped shortly after, matching Opus-level performance at Haiku pricing.
Feb 25, 2025Claude 3.7 Sonnet
Training-technique shift: Anthropic's first hybrid-reasoning model — a single model that can answer instantly or switch into visible, extended step-by-step thinking, with API-level control over how long it thinks. Launched alongside Claude Code, a command-line agentic coding tool — Anthropic's direct answer to the reasoning-model fork this site's GPT lineage traces through o1.
Era 2 — Claude 4 to Claude 4.5

The First "Critical"-Tier Safety Activation

Claude Opus 4 & Sonnet 4May 22, 2025
Research Trigger
Push agentic coding and long-horizon task reliability further, while capability growth made a higher safety tier newly relevant.
Learning Technique & Scaffolding
Extended thinking with tool use, parallel tool execution, and substantially improved long-term memory; 65% less likely to take shortcuts on agentic tasks than Sonnet 3.7.
Training Technique
Extended-thinking token budgets up to 64K reasoning tokens, lifting AIME 2025 math accuracy from ~33% to 75% (Opus 4), and up to 90% with additional test-time computation.
Safety Framework / ASL Classification
The first Anthropic model release to activate ASL-3 Deployment and Security Standards — increased protection against model-weight theft and misuse for CBRN weapons, as a precautionary measure rather than a confirmed capability threshold crossing.
Influence on Next
Set the ASL-3 baseline every subsequent Claude release (4.1, 4.5, the 5.x line, and the Mythos-class tier) has maintained or built on.
Aug 5, 2025Claude Opus 4.1
Incremental refinement: faster tool-use response times and improved function-calling stability, still within the 200,000-token context window and the ASL-3 baseline Opus 4 established.
Sep 2025Claude Sonnet 4.5
Balanced-tier refinement: continued the Sonnet line's role as the speed/capability balance point, closing further ground on Opus-tier agentic coding performance.
Era 3 — Sonnet/Opus 5 and the Mythos-Class Tier

A New Tier Appears Above Opus

Claude Fable 5 & Claude Mythos 5Jun 9, 2026
Research Trigger
A genuinely new capability tier — internally developed under "Project Glasswing" — that Anthropic judged needed a distinct name and a distinct safety architecture, not just a new version number.
Learning Technique & Scaffolding
Fable and Mythos are reportedly identical models apart from their safeguards: Fable auto-redirects requests its classifiers flag as relating to cybersecurity, biology/chemistry, or model distillation to a less-capable fallback (Claude Opus), while Mythos is a separately access-controlled, government-adjacent variant without that redirect.
Safety Framework / ASL Classification
A twin-model, classifier-based safety-redirect architecture layered on top of the existing ASL framework — a structurally new approach to containment, distinct from GPT-6 Astra's isolation-and-monitoring-based approach to a comparable problem.
Influence on Next
Established "Mythos-class" as a tier sitting above the numbered Opus/Sonnet line, continued one update later with Fable 5.1/Mythos 5.1.
Jun 30, 2026Claude Sonnet 5
Numbered-tier continuation: the most advanced intermediate model to date, aiming for Opus-adjacent performance at Sonnet-tier speed and pricing — the numbered Opus/Sonnet line continuing to advance independently of the new Mythos-class tier above it.
Jul 24, 2026Claude Opus 5
Numbered-tier flagship: a step-change over Opus 4.8, described by reporting at the time as approaching Fable 5's frontier intelligence without fully matching it — making explicit, for the first time in this lineage, a public two-tier frontier structure (Mythos-class above, numbered Opus below).
Claude Fable 5.1 & Claude Mythos 5.1Sep 1, 2026
Learning Technique & Scaffolding
Continued refinement of the Fable/Mythos twin-model safety-redirect architecture introduced in June 2026.
Training Technique
Reported 52.6% on Terminal-Bench-Science, an agentic-science benchmark.
Compute
Undisclosed, as always — though a 75% reduction in Fable cache-read pricing was disclosed as a deployment-cost change.
Influence on Next
The most recent entry in this lineage at the time of writing — released roughly two weeks before this article.
Cross-Cutting Threads

Three Patterns Across the Whole Lineage

Thread 1 — Disclosure: A Flat Line, Not a Decline Every GPT article in this project tracks a decline from full transparency to near-total opacity. Claude's lineage has no equivalent arc: architecture, parameter counts, and training compute have been undisclosed since Claude 1's very first release in March 2023, and remain undisclosed through Fable 5.1 in September 2026. There was never a transparent era to decline from.
Thread 2 — Scaffolding: From Constitutional AI to Twin-Model Safety Redirects Human-feedback RLHF (Claude 1) → Constitutional AI self-critique layered on top (Claude 1–2) → vision (Claude 3) → Artifacts and computer use (Claude 3.5) → hybrid visible reasoning (Claude 3.7) → agentic memory and tool use at ASL-3 (Claude 4) → a classifier-based twin-model safety redirect as its own architectural layer (Fable/Mythos). Each step added a new kind of scaffolding without ever changing what was disclosed about the base model underneath it.
Thread 3 — Safety Framework: From Unnamed to a New Tier's Own Architecture No named framework (Claude 1–2) → the Responsible Scaling Policy and ASL system in place by Claude 3 → the first real ASL-3 activation (Claude 4, May 2025) → a structurally new safety approach (classifier-based redirect to a fallback model) introduced alongside an entirely new capability tier (Fable/Mythos, June 2026). Safety architecture in this lineage didn't just get stricter — it got structurally more inventive as capability grew.
Claude vs. GPT

Two Labs, Two Different Disclosure Philosophies

Placing this lineage next to this site's GPT Lineage comparison makes the contrast concrete rather than abstract.

DimensionGPT Lineage (OpenAI)Claude Lineage (Anthropic)
Architecture disclosure trendFull transparency (GPT-1–3) → total opacity (GPT-4 onward)Undisclosed from the first release onward — no decline, because there was no starting transparency
Named safety frameworkPreparedness Framework, introduced alongside growing capability concernsResponsible Scaling Policy / AI Safety Levels (ASL), introduced after two frameworkless releases
First "top-tier risk" classificationGPT-6 Astra — "Critical" cybersecurity capability (Sep 2026)Claude Opus 4/Sonnet 4 — ASL-3 activation (May 2025), over a year earlier
Multi-model product structureGPT-5's real-time router between a fast and a deep-reasoning modelClaude 3.7's single hybrid-reasoning model; Fable/Mythos's twin safety-redirect models
Team creditAuthor counts (4 → 6 → 31) until GPT-4, then uncountable contributor listsNever a numbered author list for any model — company-credited from day one
OpenAI's opacity was a choice made over time. Anthropic's opacity was the starting position. Both labs ended up in roughly the same place — but they arrived from opposite directions.
What Stayed Constant

The One Thread That Never Broke Here Either

Every Claude model across fourteen named releases remains, as far as any public source confirms, a Transformer-based language model trained via next-token prediction, refined with RLHF and Constitutional-AI-style techniques. Exactly like the GPT lineage, the foundational architecture family was never the interesting variable — what changed was scaffolding, safety architecture, and product shape, layered repeatedly on top of a base nobody outside Anthropic has ever been shown in detail.

⚠️ What's Missing or Uncertain

Every release after Claude 2 in this article is covered at bridge depth, not full case-study depth — consistent with the "consolidated comparison, skipping individual case studies" scope of this piece. Undisclosed cells reflect genuine gaps in Anthropic's own public materials. Several exact dates and figures for the most recent releases (Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Fable 5.1/Mythos 5.1) come from reporting very close to this article's writing date and should be checked against Anthropic's own current documentation for anything time-sensitive, such as pricing.

🧭 Closing — Opacity as a Starting Position, Not an Ending One

🎯 The Bottom Line
Anthropic's fourteen-release, three-and-a-half-year lineage never had an open era to lose — its entire story had to be told through capability, scaffolding, and safety architecture instead of a shrinking disclosure trail. Constitutional AI, the ASL framework's first real activation a year ahead of GPT-6 Astra's comparable milestone, and the genuinely novel Fable/Mythos twin-model safety redirect are the through-line here — proof that a lab can build an entirely legible public safety narrative around a model it has never technically described in detail, which is precisely the opposite lesson the GPT lineage teaches.
